kitDescription: D: Killer Wife is a Fire-element Sniper Rifle Supporter on Burst I whose whole kit is paced by her own full-charge shots. Every 8 full charges she knocks 7 seconds off the whole team's Burst Skill cooldowns, and every 5 full charges she gives the team a 5.06% Attack Damage buff for 10 seconds, so the team bursts noticeably more often and hits harder throughout the fight. Whenever the team enters Full Burst she gives herself and any other Sniper Rifle allies 13.55% Pierce Damage for 10 seconds, and every third of her own full charges she gains Pierce for a single shot. Her burst fires a 269.28%-of-final-ATK hit at the enemy nearest her crosshair and marks it with Wipe Out for 10 seconds. While that mark is up, allies shooting the marked enemy get a buff chosen by where they hit: body hits grant an ATK bonus worth 12.19% of her own ATK, while hits on destructible parts instead grant 16.26% increased core damage — the test boss has no parts, so in practice only the body-hit ATK buff is ever earned.

redAssertions: fixture non-vacuity: 'her burst really casts' — asserts applies(coreDamagePct,16.26).length > 0; the driver deliberately deleted the parts branch, so the blind writer's chosen witness cannot exist. Non-gotcha (witness choice, not driver error): the burst provably casts via the 269.28 nuke (13 casts) and the body-branch casterAtkPct (13 cast frames × 3 allies) in the driver test W5/W7.

burst B 'parts branch: coreDamagePct 16.26 to allies' — same deleted branch. Non-gotcha and in fact the CORRECT direction: kit says 'Allies that hit PARTS'; the partless scope-lock boss can never earn it, and the pre-2026-07-17 ungated encoding lifted every ally's core bucket (driver test W6 counterfactual cfPartsReadded confirms all three totals rise). Removal is the faithful choice; blind S6's own caveat concedes the strict reading is inert.

S1a 'gainPierce effect on a chargeCounter:3 self block' — driver leaves the line unmodeled. Non-gotcha: recorded verbatim in unmodeled.skill1 + a caveat naming the effect (small own-damage undercount via the 13.55% Pierce Damage-Up), so DOCUMENTED_GAP, not SILENT_DROP. The blind test's own inertness assertion (teammates byte-identical without the tag) PASSES.

S2a 'trigger.kind === chargeCounter' (got hitCount) — primitive-name over-specification. An SR always full-charges on auto (mechanics §4: einkk NikkeFullChargeMode.always), so hitCount 8 counts exactly the same events as chargeCounter 8. All behavioral assertions in the same describe block (repeating burstCdr seconds:7, allies target, rotation acceleration, 8-vs-5 threshold load-bearing) pass. RECON_ERROR-class, not a faithfulness error.

S2b 'trigger.kind === chargeCounter' + 'chargeCounter counts set == {3,5,8}' (got hitCount, and no 3-counter since S1a is unmodeled) — same primitive-name issue plus the documented S1a gap. Bucket/value/target/duration assertions all pass.

burst B body branch 'vals.size === 1' (got 2) — blind-test fixture leak: it filters casterAtkPct by `value > 12.19*10` but never isolates by caster, so crown's own kit casterAtkPct enters the set. The driver test W7 pins the single flat value to (12.19/100)×d-killer-wife.staticAtk with casterIdx isolation and passes. Blind-test defect, not a driver defect.

skill1.kitLine: Full Charge x3: self Gain Pierce 1 shot
skill1.driverSaid: Not modeled; both prose lines copied verbatim into unmodeled.skill1 + a caveat stating the effect and the cost (a tagged shot would become eligible for the 13.55% Pierce Damage-Up during Full Burst → small own-damage undercount). Driver test W1 PINS the skip: the skill1 slot emits EXACTLY {pierceDamagePct} and no self pierce-tag/damage stat.
skill1.blindSaid: S2b called it FIX (needs a step-gated gainPierce, not hasPierce); S6 modeled it as chargeCounter:3 → gainPierce durationSec 1.2 with its own ⚑ that 1.2s is an unmeasured stand-in for a one-shot window; S5 asserted the effect exists (RED) but its own inertness assertion passed.
skill1.formulaCheck: damage-calculation.md §11/§1e: Pierce Damage ▲ is a Damage-Up-bucket term gated on a live pierce tag; game-mechanics.md §11: pierce core+body double-hits are a MULTI-PART-boss mechanic and PIERCE_CORE_DOUBLE=false on the partless test boss. So on the v1 boss the tag adds no targets and no doubling; the only lost value is the Damage-Up eligibility of one shot per 3 charges during FB windows.
skill1.explanation: Deliberate within-slot skip, verbatim-recorded, with direction+magnitude of the undercount and the blocking primitive named (gainPierce has durationSec only, no durationShots — S6 independently hit the same wall and had to invent an unmeasured 1.2s). Modeling it would require an unmeasured constant, which is exactly what the ⚑ discipline forbids shipping silently. Tier: v1-partless / missing-primitive. Not a SILENT_DROP — the slot itself is live (it emits W2).

skill1.kitLine: FB enter: SR allies Pierce Dmg 13.55%
skill1.driverSaid: fullBurstEnter → alliesOfWeapon{weapon:'SR'} → buff pierceDamagePct 13.55 durationSec 10. Test W2 pins value 13.55, distinctFrames === fbFrames (once per FB entry, 6/fight), duration 600f, targets exactly {d-killer-wife, helm} and never crown (MG).
skill1.blindSaid: S6 identical block (fullBurstEnter / alliesOfWeapon SR / 13.55 / 10s). S2b independently ruled FAITHFUL with the same target set and the same 'self INCLUDED, no except-self clause' reading. S5's three behavioral assertions on this line all GREEN.
skill1.formulaCheck: damage-calculation.md §1e — Pierce Damage ▲ is a Damage-Up additive term, correct bucket. Trigger identity matches the prose 'Activates when entering Full Burst' (fullBurstEnter, ANY team FB — not burstCast); mechanics §8 confirms entry auras resolve at window open. Weapon scoping matches 'Affects all allies with a Sniper Rifle'.
skill1.explanation: Three-way convergence (driver = S6 = S2b) on trigger, target scope, magnitude and duration, and the driver carries the discriminating counterfactual (cfPierceAll: the pre-2026-07-20 all-allies encoding reaches the MG). Fires 6× over 180s. NOTE for the owner: the buff APPLIES correctly but is currently damage-inert in this comp because no ally holds a live pierce tag (S1a unmodeled; grave-style tags exist only in other comps) — that inertness is the S1a gap's consequence, not a defect in this line's encoding, and both S5 and the driver caveat say so.

skill2.kitLine: Full Charge x8: allies Burst CD -7s
skill2.driverSaid: hitCount count:8 → allies → burstCdr seconds:7, recurring (no oncePerBattle). Test W3 pins the bounded outcome (6 team Full Bursts) and discriminates against the 2026-07-16 parser bug (shotFired → CDR every shot) which floods cooldowns into strictly MORE Full Bursts.
skill2.blindSaid: S6 chargeCounter:8 / allies / burstCdr 7 — same magnitude, target, recurrence. S5 RED on the primitive NAME only; its behavioral assertions (repeating, seconds 7, allies, rotation acceleration, 8-vs-5 threshold load-bearing) all GREEN. S2b ruled FAITHFUL with the same recurring reading.
skill2.formulaCheck: Not a damage bucket — burst-cooldown economy, correctly outside the §1 product. mechanics §8: burst cooldowns gate the rotation, so the observable is FB cadence, which is what W3 asserts. hitCount vs chargeCounter is behaviorally identical here: game-mechanics.md §4/§7 — auto always full-charges (einkk NikkeFullChargeMode.always), so every one of her pulls IS a full charge; S2b's own spec conceded 'SR always full-charges in-sim so hitCount≈chargeCounter'.
skill2.explanation: ~13 firings over 105 shots (floor(105/8)), i.e. roughly once per rotation — matching the prose cadence and the community read cited in the note. The 8-threshold is proven load-bearing by both the driver's shotFired counterfactual and S5's count:5 counterfactual. The hitCount-vs-chargeCounter divergence is a RECON_ERROR-class naming preference with zero behavioral consequence for an always-full-charging SR.

skill2.kitLine: Full Charge x5: allies Atk dmg 5.06% 10s
skill2.driverSaid: hitCount count:5 → allies → buff attackDamagePct 5.06 durationSec 10. Test W4 pins distinctFrames === floor(shots/5) = 21 firings, 3 targets per firing, duration 600f, and discriminates against the hitCount-1 parser-bug class.
skill2.blindSaid: S6 chargeCounter:5 / allies / attackDamagePct 5.06 / 10s — identical bucket, value, target, duration. S2b ruled FAITHFUL and explicitly named the nearest-wrong as atkPct. S5 GREEN on bucket ('never atkPct'), on all-four-ally reach, on finite window, and on the self-scope counterfactual; RED only on trigger.kind naming.
skill2.formulaCheck: damage-calculation.md §1e — 'Attack damage ▲' is the attackDamagePct term of the DamageUp bucket, NOT the ATK% term inside FinalATK (§1a). Encoding it as atkPct would put it in a different bucket with different dilution against the comp's other ATK buffs; the driver and both blinds agree on attackDamagePct, and S5's `applies(atkPct, 5.06).length === 0` assertion is GREEN.
skill2.explanation: 21 firings × 3 allies over the fight, refreshing a 10s window on a ~5-shot cadence → near-continuous uptime after the opening magazine, exactly as the note claims. First application is gated behind 5 real shots (never frame 0), satisfying S2b's inertness requirement. Counter independence from the 8-counter is proven behaviorally by the two separate blocks and by W3's/W4's separate cadences.

burst.driverSaid: burstCast → enemy → flatDamage atkPct 269.28 (no core, no explicit noFb). Test W5 pins exactly one burst-bucket damage event per cast (13), the lv10 magnitude, and fbMajorApplied === false on every one; discriminates against the lv1 magnitude 159.12.
burst.blindSaid: S6 identical except an explicit noFb:true, which its own caveat labels 'follows the burst-cast pre-FB convention, not a measurement'. S2b ruled FAITHFUL, named the nearest-wrong as fullBurstEnter-keying or fbMajorApplied true. S5 GREEN on magnitude, on core:false, on 'real damage for HER, inert for everyone else'.
burst.formulaCheck: damage-calculation.md §1b Full Burst timing rule + game-mechanics.md §8: burst-cast damage lands 22f BEFORE the FB countdown starts, so it takes neither the +0.5 nor entry auras — the engine forces this by TIMING (noFb forced for burst-cast direct damage). The driver's implicit reliance on that engine convention is verified empirically by W5's fbMajorApplied===false assertion, and S6's explicit noFb:true would be a redundant second application of the same exemption. Skill-damage rules (§2b): crits, never cores, never range — driver sets core:false and adds no range; correct. Level-10 value 269.28 matches description_value_list index 9 exactly.
burst.explanation: 13 casts / 13 nuke events — one per her own burstCast, never keyed to fullBurstEnter (the fixture's cast frames are provably distinct from FB-start frames, per the driver's fixture-sanity assertion). Magnitude is the prose's own lv10 number, not a fitted value, so it is out of magnitude scope per Section 1F.

burst.kitLine: Inflicts Wipe Out on target 10 sec
burst.driverSaid: Same burstCast/enemy block: effect targetStatus {name:'Wipe Out', durationSec:10}, authored ahead of the gated rider block so the same-frame gate reads a status written earlier that frame (block order documented as load-bearing in both the note and the caveat).
burst.blindSaid: S6 identical (targetStatus 'wipeOut', 10s, on the enemy-targeted burst block) — name-key spelling differs but is self-consistent within each file. S2b ruled FAITHFUL and named the nearest-wrong as modeling it as a damageTakenPct debuff. S5 GREEN: enemy-targeted block, durationSec 10, name matches /wipe\s*out/i, and the gate is live BOTH ways.
burst.formulaCheck: No damage bucket — a named enemy status with zero direct contribution, which is correct: the prose gives Wipe Out no damage-taken or defensive term, it exists only as the gate for the two area riders. Any damageTakenPct encoding would have invented a §1g Taken-bucket term the prose never grants; the driver emits none.
burst.explanation: Inflicted on each of her 13 casts; the 10s window is measured from HER cast, not from FB start, matching the prose. Damage-inert by itself, as required. The gate it opens is exercised 13× (W7).

burst.kitLine: hit parts: core dmg 16.26% for 10 sec
burst.driverSaid: Removed from the effects array (2026-07-17 parts-branch fix). Recorded in unmodeled.burst with the reason, plus two caveats carrying the full ⚑ triple — ESTIMATE: 'small own-comp core bucket', out-of-domain on the v1 partless boss; RECIPE: 'wire it as requiresTargetStatus "Wipe Out" + requiresCore (parts→core proxy) + a parts-hit trigger when parts enter scope'; TIER: SKIPPED-CONDITIONAL / out-of-domain / v1-partless, cf. brid's Wind-Code debuffs. Test W6 PINS the skip (burst slot emits no coreDamagePct) and discriminates with cfPartsReadded, which makes coreDamagePct appear and lifts all three totals.
burst.blindSaid: S2b ruled it a GAP with the same logic: 'the scope-lock boss is PARTLESS, so the real trigger condition never occurs in v1 … deleting this line moves totals by exactly 0'; it warned that any core proxy is a CALIBRATED encoding decision, not prose, since parts ≠ core. S6 DID model it (requiresCore + requiresTargetStatus) but its own caveat says 'a strict reading would leave the parts branch fully inert … this dual model can OVER-CREDIT when core exposure is high' and its recipe says to drop it to unmodeled when per-hitter targeting is impossible — i.e. S6's strict reading converges on the driver's removal.
burst.formulaCheck: game-mechanics.md §11 + the test-boss-has-no-parts constraint: the scope-lock boss is partless and hit LOCATION never changes a value — only core vs non-core. 'Damage dealt when attacking core ▲' is a coreBonus term inside the §1b Major bracket, so an ungated grant inflates every ally's core bucket at coreHitRate 1 — a real over-credit, confirmed by the driver's own cfPartsReadded run. Since the earning CONDITION (a parts hit) is unreachable, encoding the EFFECT is inventing an unearned buff, which §4 of the mechanics discipline forbids.
burst.explanation: The removal is the faithful call and is the strictly conservative one (it can only under-credit, and by exactly zero on a partless boss). Both blind agents' strict readings agree; only S6's shipped-but-self-flagged dual model differs. The ⚑ carries estimate + recipe + tier as required. This is the line the two S5 reds (#1, #5) hang on — the blind test picked a witness the driver correctly deleted.

burst.kitLine: hit body: ATK 12.19% of user's ATK 10s
burst.driverSaid: burstCast → allies → buff casterAtkPct 12.19 durationSec 10, gated on requiresTargetStatus 'Wipe Out' ONLY. The stranded requiresCore:true was REMOVED (2026-07-25 fix). Test W7 pins: one firing per own cast (13 frames === castFrames), all 3 allies, 600f window, value === (12.19/100)×d-killer-wife.staticAtk to 6 places, and the new GATE-DIRECTION assertion — identical application count at coreHitRate 0 and 1.
burst.blindSaid: S6 also placed requiresCore on the PARTS branch and left the body branch gated on the status alone — an INDEPENDENT corroboration of exactly this fix (its body block: hitCount:1 / allies / requiresTargetStatus 'wipeOut', no requiresCore). S2b ruled FIX and named both nearest-wrongs the driver avoids: stat atkPct instead of casterAtkPct, and leaving it ungated/permanent. S5's only red here is the crown-contaminated vals.size filter, not the encoding.
burst.formulaCheck: damage-calculation.md §1a: 'ATK ▲ X% of caster's ATK' converts at apply time to a FLAT add of the caster's staticAtk × X, sitting OUTSIDE the recipient's (1+ATK%) sum — exactly what casterAtkPct does and what W7's staticAtk assertion proves; a plain atkPct would dilute into the sum and over-credit the high-ATK carry. On the gate: mechanics/§1b model the partless boss as core-vs-non-core only, so 'Allies that hit the BODY' == a NON-core hit. requiresCore therefore INVERTED the kit condition — it made the body buff require the one hit class the kit excludes. Removing it is the faithful direction: the branch is now maximally live at coreHitRate 0 (where every hit is a body hit) and unchanged at coreHitRate 1, which is exactly what the new W7 assertion pins.
burst.explanation: REAL-GOTCHA RESOLVED. The fix is confirmed on all four prescribed points: (1) requiresCore is absent from the body block in the shipped override; (2) W7's third assertion now pins the correct DIRECTION (identical app counts at coreHitRate 0 and 1) and would go red if requiresCore were re-added, since the gate would zero it at coreHitRate 0; (3) the proxy note is re-pointed onto the parked parts branch in both the note and the caveat, where it belongs once destructible parts are modeled; (4) board movement at the scope-lock basis (coreHitRate 1) is zero — the branch fired before and after — while the coreHitRate 0 smoke basis correctly moves 54.6M→57.1M, which is the faithful direction, not a regression. One documented residual: the surviving requiresTargetStatus gate is in-fixture-neutral (her burst always inflicts Wipe Out same-frame), so it is documented rather than asserted as a damage discriminator; that is a coverage note, not an unfaithfulness.

verdictRationale: GO. The single REAL-GOTCHA from the prior pass (ENCODING, low — the stranded requiresCore:true on the burst body branch, a parts→core proxy left behind when the parts branch was deleted on 2026-07-17) is fully resolved: the shipped override's body block is now gated on requiresTargetStatus 'Wipe Out' alone, which matches the kit's 'Allies that hit the BODY' == non-core on the partless scope-lock boss, and the driver test W7 no longer merely restates the encoding — it pins the DIRECTION (identical application counts at coreHitRate 0 and 1), so a regression re-adding requiresCore fails at coreHitRate 0 rather than passing vacuously. The fix is corroborated independently, not just self-consistently: the blind S6 override (written from prose alone, before the fix) had already placed requiresCore on the PARTS branch and left the body branch status-gated only — the same conclusion reached by a different route. Board impact is the faithful shape: byte-identical at the scope-lock basis (coreHitRate 1, where the branch fired both before and after) and correctly larger on validate-overrides' coreHitRate 0 smoke basis (54.6M→57.1M), which is the branch coming live where the kit says it should be maximally live. All eight kit lines now grade FAITHFUL (6) or DOCUMENTED_GAP (2) = 1.0; both gaps carry the full ⚑ triple (S1a gainPierce: estimate 'small own-damage undercount via the 13.55% Pierce Damage-Up', recipe 'needs a durationShots primitive — gainPierce has durationSec only', tier v1-partless/missing-primitive; parts branch: estimate 'small own-comp core bucket', recipe 'requiresTargetStatus Wipe Out + requiresCore proxy + a parts-hit trigger', tier out-of-domain/v1-partless), and both are recorded verbatim in `unmodeled` rather than silently dropped. Convergence is mechanically RED (6 of 26 S5 assertions), but every red re-classifies as non-gotcha and I confirm the prior rulings: reds #1 and #5 assert a coreDamagePct witness the driver correctly DELETED (the ungated parts branch was a live all-ally core-bucket over-credit on a boss where no ally can ever earn it — the driver's own cfPartsReadded counterfactual proves it lifts all three totals, and S6's own caveat concedes the strict reading is inert); red #2 targets a documented, verbatim-recorded inert-line omission whose own inertness assertion passes; reds #3/#4 are primitive-NAME over-specification (hitCount vs chargeCounter is behaviorally identical for an SR that always full-charges on auto, per mechanics §4/§7, and every behavioral assertion in those blocks is green); red #6 is a blind-test fixture leak that fails to isolate by caster and so picks up crown's own casterAtkPct. Discrimination holds: each load-bearing line carries a counterfactual that fails under its nearest-wrong model — all-allies pierce reaching the MG, shotFired CDR flooding cooldowns into strictly more Full Bursts, hitCount-1 attack damage over-firing, the lv1 159.12 nuke magnitude, the re-added ungated parts branch, and now the coreHitRate-0 gate-direction probe. SAME-MODEL RESIDUAL FOR OWNER SPOT-CHECK, in priority order: (1) the surviving requiresTargetStatus 'Wipe Out' gate on the body branch is in-fixture-NEUTRAL — her burst always inflicts the status on the same frame the gated block fires, so no test in this suite would catch that gate being dropped entirely; it is documented, not asserted, and only matters for the future parts wiring or a comp where the status could be absent. (2) The 13.55% Pierce Damage buff applies correctly but is currently damage-INERT in this comp, because the only pierce tag this unit self-sources is the S1a line that is deliberately unmodeled — the S1a gap and the S1b line are coupled, and closing S1a would need a measured one-shot window (S6 had to invent an unmeasured 1.2s), so the honest gap is the right call but the owner should know the pair currently contributes nothing to her own damage here. (3) Every full-charge threshold (3/5/8) rides the datamined cadence tuple (chargeFrames 60 / reloadFrames 141 / ammo 6), which S6 flagged ⚑ — the burstCdr firing rate and the 5.06% uptime are only as good as that tuple, and both blinds and the driver share it, so agreement there is not independent evidence. Magnitudes are prose-sourced lv10 values throughout (13.55 / 7 / 5.06 / 269.28 / 16.26 / 12.19), none tuned to hit the board.
